sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, Azure Policy exemption structure
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: an exemption exempts a resource hierarchy or resource from evaluation; category 'Waiver: the non-compliance state of the resource is temporarily accepted' (and can exclude a resource from one or more definitions in an initiative, not the whole initiative), 'Mitigated: the policy intent is met through another method'; expiresOn, after which the exemption 'is no longer honored' but is kept for record; scope at or under the assignment scope; policyDefinitionReferenceId is an array naming the initiative's definitions exempted; the creator needs policyExemptions/write and the exempt/Action verb on the assignment. The Azure Policy overview (read 2026-11-18): 'Even if an individual has access to perform an action, if the result is a non-compliant resource, Azure Policy still blocks the create or update'; an exemption or a change to the denying assignment is the way to allow it. The error text in the case is an authored rendering.
